In the early 1990s I was having a discussion with my fellow academics about South Africa. I expressed the naive hope that the transition to majority rule would involve a maintenance of the good elements of the apartheid state: true democracy (among the people who could vote) and a lack of the corrupt looting of the public treasury by venal politicians. My liberal-minded friends thought this was an outrageous thing to say. The 'correct' line to take is that the state had to stripped down to the frame and rebuilt along entirely different lines by the black majority. One woman was so upset that she simply got up and walked out of the room. (This, I found out, was one of the favourite tactics by western liberals when faced with dissent.) Now here we are. 

And on this subject, during the lead up to BMR in both Rhodesia and South Africa, the news source I listened to most often was the ultra-liberal CBC (Canada). They had stories on these countries virtually every day, sometimes every hourly newscast. And since BMR: crickets. I have not hear a story on CBC about either Zimbabwe or South Arica in years. Western liberals have a lot to answer for in thei treatment of this issue.
